acip: 'DI LTAR LEGS PAR BSLABS PA'I SMAN PA BDAG NYID LA NAD MED BZHIN DU YANG NA, BLTAR BSTAN NAS SMAN KHAB DANG TSA BA DAG BSTEN PAR BYAS PAS DE'I RJES SU SLOB PA'I NAD PA DAG YONGS SU SOS PAR BYED PA DE BZHIN DU DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA SMAN PA'I RGYAL PO GNOD PA THAMS CAD ZHI BAR MDZAD PAS KYANG SGRIB PA MI MNGA' NA YANG NGA'I LAS 'DI'O RNAM PAR SMIN PA NI 'DI 'O ZHES PHRIN LAS STON PAR MDZAD DE
wylie: 'di ltar legs par bslabs pa'i sman pa bdag nyid la nad med bzhin du yang na, bltar bstan nas sman khab dang tsha ba dag bsten par byas pas de'i rjes su slob pa'i nad pa dag yongs su sos par byed pa de bzhin du de bzhin gshegs pa sman pa'i rgyal po gnod pa thams cad zhi bar mdzad pas kyang sgrib pa mi mnga' na yang nga'i las 'di'o rnam par smin pa ni 'di 'o zhes phrin las ston par mdzad de
english: Think of a very well-trained physician; he may not have any kind of illness himself, but still he might let his own blood, or stick himself with a medicine needle, or apply hot steel to himself, just so his students, the sick ones who are following him, will allow him to use these same methods to cure them. The One Gone Thus, the king of all physicians, is the same. Despite the fact that he has put a stop to every harm he himself could ever undergo, and so has no possible obstacle at all, he nonetheless undertakes as one of his enlightened acts to pretend, and to say "this is my karma," and "this is my karma ripening."
